And to the many other friends that gave and continue to give love and support along the way: THANK YOU: EJ Chichilnisky, Dave Morin, David Berson, Bill Guido, Rachel Wong, Jeff Goldberg, Chris and Denise Niell, Matt Walker, Hoby Darling, Chris Voss, Rhonda Patrick, Shawn Ryan, Tom and Lisa Bilyeu, Craig and Keli Koniver, Adam Haidary, Steven Bartlett, Jay Shetty, Mark Hyman, Lewis Howes, Ben Bruno, Josh Trachtenberg, Rich Roll, Tim Ferriss, Laird Hamilton and Gabby Reece, Pat Dossett, Brooke Jaye, Mark Bell, Nsima Inyang, Derek, Rory Cordial, Peter Attia, Julia Allison, Tom Segura, Bert Kreischer, Luca Padua, DJ Shipley, Marcus and Amber Capone, Noelle Fischer, Rich and Kristen Diviney, John Joseph, Darin Olien, Orin Snyder, Jimmy Asci, Mark Kalan, Benjamin Reese, Mark Whiteley, Dusty Brown, Erik Gambatese, Larissa Martinez, Bob Peters, Ari Emmanuel and Ben Davis at WME, Justin Edbrooke and Ethan Kurtzman at CAA, Michael Kives… and on and on and on.

Immense thanks to my scientific mentors. There are really no words to express my gratitude to Harry Carlisle, Barbara Chapman, and Ben Barres for teaching me how to do science right and for being more than just mentors—for being guides for me in science and life. I miss you each and all so much.

My Portland family: Jocelyn, Henry, Nina, Sunny, Daniel: for all the encouragement, laughs, and love.

Deanna F., for all your care and guidance. Incalculable.

Emmy, Baya, Lennon, for your love and support. Huge love for you now and forever.

Stanford and Stanford Medicine, for being so supportive of the HLP and for being such pillars of excellence. It’s an extraordinary thing to be surrounded by so many brilliant and mission-driven people.

The members of the “original” Huberman Lab—the staff, students, postdocs, and all those who came through and contributed to the experiments and culture of hard work and playful discovery. I am immensely grateful for your (often heroic) efforts and for you each as people as well.

Aunt Sue, for your love and all the animal photos and advice on life. I am blessed to have you in my corner and I love you.

Rick, Dan, Gena, Maddie, for your love and support and always being there to encourage.

And all the Argentine relatives for the love and messages, laughter and reminders to come visit in Buenos Aires.

Mom, for instilling in me a desire and drive to help the world, not just because one can and should but because we feel we absolutely must.

Dad, for instilling in me a love of science and discovery.

Mike, for your encouragement and support. Mette, for your encouragement and support.

Isabel, for helping me research HLP episodes, the eye rolls, for making family gatherings so joyful, and for your dry sense of humor.

Lara, for the laughs and love, loyalty, and friendship. Love you, Leff. Emily, for your love, your seemingly endless patience and support, your optics on people and life that only someone as grounded, calm, and yet observant could possibly have. For being so genuinely kind and expressing your wish to make life easier for me. I am so blessed to have you and Nino and Strummer in my life.

All the HLP guests: Thank you for sharing so much valuable knowledge with the public, for trusting me to showcase your voices, and for allowing me to be in the role of student. I am truly blessed to be able to sit and learn from you much less to be able to share that with so many people.

HLP listeners and readers of this book: Thank you for embracing the material—including my occasional stumbling and perpetual lack of succinctness. I appreciate your openness to science, to protocols, to learning, and to your commitment to improving yourself and, in doing so, the world.

God. Acknowledging out loud that I am a scientist who also has faith was once scary.

No more. Thank you.

## About the Author

![Andrew D. Huberman](images/andrew-huberman.jpeg)

Andrew D. Huberman, PhD, is a neuroscientist and tenured professor in the departments of neurobiology and ophthalmology and, by courtesy, psychiatry and behavioral sciences at Stanford School of Medicine. He has made numerous significant contributions to the fields of brain development, brain function, and neural plasticity. His laboratory at Stanford School of Medicine has published work in top journals such as *Nature, Science*, and *Cell* and in top media outlets like the BBC, *Time, Scientific American*, and Discover. Huberman is a McKnight Foundation and Pew Foundation Fellow and was awarded the Association for Research in Vision and Ophthalmology’s Cogan Award in 2017, given to the scientist making the most significant discoveries in the study of vision. In 2021, Andrew launched the *Huberman Lab* podcast, which consistently ranks as the top health and fitness podcast in the world and has consistently ranked in the top ten podcasts globally.
